text:
Boston arrives in Los Angeles on the second night of a back-to-back, off a 4-2 win in Anaheim, while the Kings have had three days of rest. The model has it close, 3.00 expected goals for LAK and 2.87 for BOS. The chance-creation numbers are close too: BOS sits at 3.05 expected goals for and against per 60, LAK at 2.69 for and 2.54 against. At five on five BOS has taken 54% of the expected goals and LAK 51%. On special teams, LAK's power play is the stronger unit (0.71 expected goals a game to 0.50), and BOS takes 4.9 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side chances.

The goalie matchup favors Boston, though the sample is thin. Michael DiPietro is the projected starter over Jeremy Swayman, with a .912 save percentage and +1.32 goals saved above expected in two games this season, and +0.10 in one game last year. Darcy Kuemper is projected for LAK at .847 and -5.26 this season, after -6.77 across 50 games last year. That gap is the clearest edge either side has.

Form points toward Boston, but the chances only partly agree. The Bruins are 4-1-0 in their last five with 51% of the expected goals, while the Kings are 0-3-2 with the same 51%, so LAK's slide looks more like bad luck than bad play. Los Angeles is also without Mats Zuccarello, on injured reserve. For players, Adrian Kempe has the best goal chance on the board at 37%, with Artemi Panarin at 33% to score and 67% to record a point. For BOS, David Pastrnak is at 29% to score and 66% for a point, riding a four-game point streak.
